newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: POWER BEAT BATTERY TO GO ON SALE IN NZ IN OCTOBER.
newsitem.headline: POWER BEAT BATTERY TO GO ON SALE IN NZ IN OCTOBER.

text.p: Power Beat International's long-delayed "never-go-flat" battery is expected to go on sale in New Zealand in October, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Friday.
Power Beat managing director Peter Witehira said the first shipment of batteries, manufactured in Bahrain, was due in New Zealand shortly.
He expected it to be sold as part of a "controlled marketing programme" in late October.
Initially two battery sizes would be available, one for commercial vehicles such as taxis, and the other for heavy duty and four-wheel-drive vehicles.
A further two sizes for European and Asian cars would be ready next year. Prices had yet to be decided.

Power Beat has been dogged by trouble since its formation in 1989. It was involved in a long battle with Canadian firm Trend Vision Technologies and its shares were delisted from the stock exchange last year for breaching market rules.
The batteries would be sold from a centre in Mt Wellington, Auckland, but Witehira hoped to later set up a nationwide distribution chain.
He said establishing the NZ$31.25 million Bahrain plant, built by the Al Tajir Group of Dubai, had been complex and time-consuming.
"Many of the teething problems have been ironed out and we are confident that the new product will meet expectations..." he said.
